the in vitro paralysis induced in mouse lymphoid cells by exposure to high doses endotoxin of E. coli 055:B 5 is a reversible process, which is dependent on the antigen concentration and the duration of exposure.
lymphoid cells from normal mice become specifically paralyzed after exposure to high doses in vitro of detoxified endototoxin of E. coli 055:B.
the paralysis of lymphoid cells by endotoxin is a specific event that is initiated by events taking places in vitro and is dependent on the concentration and the duration of exposure of the antigen.

the regulation of antibody synthesis against E. coli endotoxin.
